facts.text: The project is remote control software for controlling, monitoring and data collection on the LPX200 laser, mimicking the Lambda Physik handheld keypad
The program opens the pyvisa resource ASRL4::INSTR and sets CR as both the write and the read termination, so the link is a line-oriented ASCII serial port
commRes sends every command with laser_instr.query and answers 'Not a valid Command' when the query raises
The status line queries MODE?, REPRATE?, HV?, EGY?, PRESSURE? and Menu?, and prints the values in Hz, kV, mJ and mbar; the third field of the Menu? reply is the gas mixture
The running modes are HV, EGY PGR and EGY NGR
The gas lines are BUFFER, HALOGEN, INERT and RARE
The RUN STOP key reads OPMODE? and writes OPMODE=OFF when it is ON, otherwise OPMODE=ON
The TRIG INT/EXT key reads TRIGGER? and writes TRIGGER=EXT when it is INT, otherwise TRIGGER=INT
The MODE key sends MODE= followed by one of the running mode names
The REP RATE key sends the REPRATE= prefix and the COUNTS SEL key sends the COUNTS= prefix
The HV key builds HV= as the prefix of the value typed on the keypad
The EGY key builds EGY= as the prefix of the value typed on the keypad
The gas routines build OPMODE=NEW FILL, OPMODE=FLUSH <line> LINE, OPMODE=PURGE <line> LINE, OPMODE=PURGE RESERVOIR and OPMODE=ENERGY CAL
The REPRATE value is specified in Hz, the HV value is the charging voltage, and the EGY value is the beam output energy specified in mJ
The RUN STOP key starts and stops laser operation; when the laser is running, pressing it immediately stops laser emission
The gas actions are required for maintenance and should only be carried out by correspondingly authorized and trained personnel
LaserData.py queries opmode?, trigger?, reprate?, hv?, egy?, pressure?, mode? and menu?, and splits the menu reply into gas menu number, wavelength and gas mixture
